findings.text: Registration helper records a NUMA memory range for a given node and marks that node as observed when recording succeeds, propagating failure status otherwise without further side effects.

Architecture NUMA entry point chooses discovery based on firmware availability, preferring firmware driven setup when allowed and otherwise falling back to a synthetic single node covering usable memory.
Firmware NUMA probe has two build variants, one that runs ACPI discovery and validates firmware table state before reporting success, and one that always reports lack of support.

Synthetic NUMA setup builds a lone node spanning the extent of physical memory, announces disabled operation and the emulated range, and leaves the subsystem marked disabled after successful registration.

Early hotplug normalization aligns kernel reservations with node boundaries, identifies nodes that hold reserved memory, and removes hotplug marking from ranges on those nodes so that entire nodes containing kernel memory become non hotpluggable.

Debug helper maintains per node processor membership by adding or removing a processor in the node map, ignoring requests without an associated node and reporting a diagnostic while leaving state unchanged when the map is absent.

Writeback statistics bundle aggregates inode queue lengths for dirty and staged work plus timestamp dirty entries, together with cumulative writeback and reclaimable contents, dirtied and written activity, and global versus per member threshold shares.

Backing device bookkeeping centers on a global guard, an advancing identifier cursor with a lookup tree root, a shared deferred work service pointer, and a debug hierarchy root for introspection entries.

Throttle view initializers distinguish global and member accounting by selecting the applicable domain, completion counters, and parent linkage, with alternate builds collapsing member views onto the global domain.

Sampling of per writeback inode queues holds the writeback list guard while walking dirty and staged queues and testing timestamp dirtiness, with cumulative counters and threshold derivation performed outside that guard.
Minimum and maximum ratio shares plus the global minimum reserve are mutated under a global spin guard with deferred interrupt exclusion, keeping per device and global accounting consistent.

Traversal of writeback members attached to a backing device relies on read side protection combined with per member reference acquisition, permitting temporary release around operations that may sleep while retaining safe access.
Global share query refreshes available and dirty accounting including writeback activity and then derives the calling member portion of a supplied domain limit.
Group aware share query evaluates global and member availability including writeback, derives member domain limits, and returns the member portion of its own domain limit.
Global limit query refreshes dirtyable capacity and converts configured controls into paired background and foreground page thresholds for the whole system.

Availability accounting separates global sampling of dirtyable capacity and file dirty plus optional writeback contents from member sampling that queries group file and dirty usage and then derives availability from file contents and ancestor headroom.

Dirtyable capacity starts from free pages less kernel reserves, adds file cached contents, subtracts the high memory portion when high memory is excluded from dirty accounting, and remains strictly positive.
Member availability adds local file contents to the lesser of ancestor headroom and globally clean capacity not already attributable to the member, avoiding double counting of shared clean pages.

Member threshold scales the domain limit by completion share adjusted for global minimum reserve, adds a minimum ratio allotment, grants idle members a modest floor when the domain sits below its limit with stricter devices receiving the smaller floor, and clamps the result to a maximum ratio bound.
Minimum and maximum share helpers have a bandwidth aware variant that scales configured shares by observed write bandwidth participation and a direct variant that reports configured shares unchanged.

Limit derivation interprets byte controls directly and ratio controls against available memory, reinterprets byte controls as ratios against global availability for member domains, uplifts realtime tasks, and enforces width and ordering constraints between background and foreground values.

Group usage reporting refreshes pending statistics under rate limiting, exposes dirty and writeback plus file page states, and derives headroom as the tightest remaining capacity across ancestors bounded by configured ceilings.
Group domain selection yields no separate domain for the root group and the dedicated group writeback domain for non root groups.

Debug statistics reporting snapshots global limits, aggregates per member queue lengths and activity counters, and renders device wide and per group summaries, with group thresholds reported as the lesser of global share and group share.

Debug lifecycle creates a per device directory with aggregate and per group statistics entries and removes it recursively on teardown, while alternate builds reduce all lifecycle operations to no operation stubs.

Backing device attributes accept decimal user input for read ahead size and for coarse and fine minimum ratio shares, translating read ahead by page granularity and delegating ratio changes to shared helpers that validate and account globally.

Minimum share update rejects values beyond the allowed total or above the device maximum, decreases the global reserve on reduction, and on increase admits the change only when the global reserve remains within budget.
Absence of the per node processor map is handled as a recoverable diagnostic with an error report and stack capture, without mutating membership state.
Dirty accounting guards against underflow when deducting reserves and watermarks, caps high memory contribution at total capacity, and keeps background strictly below foreground after clamping.
Subsystem exposes a default inert backing device instance, a placeholder label for unknown devices, and a shared work service for deferred writeback related work.
